title: Transfer respiratory landmarks with both CT volumes available
hypothesis: Adding full source-volume context to the same failed single-view registration case may remove depth ambiguity and permit a more accurate fresh Sol solution while retaining the same small deliverable and physical tolerances.
why_hard: The full-source condition is accepted by the user on visual review of q06 and retired as a hard-task candidate for this intended example. The historical numerical result remains a normal completed failure: 2.604 mm RMS / 6.412 mm maximum, substantially better than the earlier 2D-source result of 12.731 / 32.203 mm. Recorded code uses actual 3D patches and broad search independent of the failed global field. The practical acceptance, automated score and earlier 2D failure are distinct judgments; no repeatable difficulty claim is made.
next_action: Retain as accepted calibration with the unchanged automated result and explicit user adjudication; no further trial scheduled.

sources.note: User asked whether inputs were just 2D patches and requested a 3D version on 2026-09-16. Exact message ID is unavailable. The target already was 3D; this matched follow-up adds the full source CT.
Learn2Reg LungCT 1.11 source attribution and CC BY 4.0, using previously hash-verified local data.

notes: The only added public file is reference_volume.npz. Existing view, query pixels, nominal geometry, target CT, answers, grader, tolerances and resources are unchanged. Every original source-view pixel independently matches a reslice of the new volume. The model gets no prior answers or solver and no hidden labels. The predeclared 3D author patch method fails, while the unchanged 2D method reproduces its exact passing answer inside the enriched image. Full-source model stages are independently scored only after execution; no label-assisted rescue or candidate selection is submitted. One fresh run per condition confounds information with strategy choice and model variability. Public-label training contamination and clinical validity remain unresolved. Old evidence and concurrent work are preserved.
